independent_outcomes: Stop building a dependent on a line that lacks its prerequisite's merge: the 'merged' gate (and the plain-edge hold from #647) checks the run's line, not just the base's merge state in the host.
proposed_seams: No clean cut. The five success criteria all test one gate, and each one only means something with the same fix in place. The plain-edge hold (criterion 2) shares the check with the merged edge, so splitting it out would mean two PRs changing the same function in flow._runnable.
The docs update at docs/07-crosscutting.md:704-719 can go in the same PR. It only describes the fix, so it does not need its own PR.

If a split is wanted anyway, the least bad seam is the resumed-run carry case (a prerequisite whose PR head is already on the carried line but whose merge commit is not). The Iteration 1 notes show a false hold there. It could be handled as a follow-up once the basic check lands. This is a judgment call, not a clear boundary.
